_meta.indication: HETLIOZ is indicated for the treatment of Non-24-Hour Sleep-Wake Disorder (Non-24).

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed FDA documents
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study; 84 totally blind subjects with Non-24 randomized 1:1 to tasimelteon 20 mg or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Totally blind patients with Non-24-Hour Sleep-Wake Disorder
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: entrainment of the circadian melatonin rhythm (proportion of patients entrained, based on melatonin/aMT6s measurements)
pivotal_trials.result: Entrainment of the melatonin rhythm significantly greater with tasimelteon vs placebo (% difference = 17.4; p = 0.0171); clinical response (entrained + N24CRS >=3) % difference = 23.7; p = 0.0028

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed FDA documents
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized-withdrawal, double-masked, placebo-controlled trial; after ~11 weeks of treatment, 20 patients randomized 1:1 to continue tasimelteon 20 mg or switch to placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with Non-24 who had previously participated in/been screened in Study 3201
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Applicant's proposed primary endpoint: proportion of non-entrainment of the circadian melatonin rhythm (aMT6s); review team assessed efficacy on clinical endpoints
pivotal_trials.n: N=20 in the randomized-withdrawal phase (tasimelteon 10; placebo 10)
pivotal_trials.result: Biomarker-based primary endpoint showed a statistically significant benefit favoring tasimelteon; clinical endpoints (UQ-dTSD, MoST, CGIC, dTSD, LQ-nTST) nominally significant favoring tasimelteon

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >5% and >=2x placebo): headache (17% vs 7%), ALT increased (10% vs 5%), nightmare/abnormal dreams (10% vs 0%), upper respiratory tract infection (7% vs 0%), and urinary tract infection (7% vs 2%). Key warning: somnolence.
target_moa: Tasimelteon is a melatonin receptor (MT1/MT2) agonist that acts as a circadian regulator, entraining the master body clock to the 24-hour day in totally blind patients with Non-24
modality: Small molecule (oral capsule; molecular formula C15H19NO2, MW 245.32)

rems.type: The DRISK team agreed there were no serious risks identified to warrant a REMS

advisory_committee.vote: The Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee met November 14, 2013; voted that substantial evidence of efficacy was presented (YES=10, NO=0, ABSTAIN=1) and that safety was adequately addressed (YES=11, NO=0, ABSTAIN=0)

description.text: Added indication for nighttime sleep disturbances in Smith-Magenis Syndrome (SMS) in patients 16 years of age and older

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the addition of nighttime sleep disturbances in Smith-Magenis Syndrome (SMS) in patients 16 years of age and older.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation granted 1/9/10 (also cited as 1/19/10) for the treatment of Non-24-Hour Disorder in blind individuals with no light perception

citations.quote: Orphan drug designation for the treatment of Non-24-Hour Disorder in blind individuals with no light perception was granted on 1/9/10.
On 1/19/10, the Agency granted orphan-drug designation of tasimelteon for Non-24 Hour Disorder in blind individuals without light perception.

summary.text: Tasimelteon (HETLIOZ) received orphan drug designation for Non-24-Hour Disorder in blind individuals with no light perception and was reviewed as a Priority NDA; it was the first drug approved for Non-24, a novel indication for which no drug was previously approved. No REMS was required.

citations.quote: Orphan drug designation for the treatment of Non-24-Hour Disorder in blind individuals with no light perception was granted on 1/9/10.

Application Type P
Application Number(s) NDA 205677
Priority or Standard Priority

Vanda Pharmaceuticals submitted NDA 205,677 to support marketing of tasimelteon, a melatonin agonist, for the treatment of Non-24 hour sleep-wake disorder (Non-24) in totally blind patients. This is a novel indication, for which no drug is currently approved.
The DRISK team agrees that there are no serious risks identified at this time to warrant a REMS.
